title: LED-matrix RED alarm row never blinks and is usually blank (blink phase aliased by the 250 ms redraw)
description: matrix_service() redraws every kMxPeriodMs = 250 ms (line 1452, 1520), and the loop polls far faster than 1 ms, so draws land exactly 250 ms apart. Row 7 for RED uses ((now / kAlarmRedHalfMs) & 1) with kAlarmRedHalfMs = 125 ms (line 1505). floor((t0 + 250k)/125) = floor(t0/125) + 2k, so the parity never changes. Row 7 is therefore either lit all the time or dark all the time, depending on the phase of the first draw. It only flips after a loop stall moves the phase. The link-down flash at line 1482 (kLinkDownHalfMs = 100 ms) aliases to a 1 Hz pattern, not the 'fast like the ALARM lamp' the comment at lines 1444-1446 promises. The harness check 'RED = 13 blinking' (tools/host_test/station/test_e22.cpp:237) calls matrix_frame() at hand-picked times (+700 ms / +100 ms), not at the redraw cadence, so it cannot see the aliasing.
failure_scenario: Reproduced with the real sketch compiled against the station harness (scratch /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/5ee836b4-fd12-52ad-8530-d6659d1475b9/scratchpad/review31/gs/alias_test.cpp). Send S|1|2|0|0 (RED), then call matrix_service() every 1 ms for 20 s. Result: 'row 7 all lit in 0 frames, dark in 80 frames'. During a RED alarm the matrix alarm row is empty, which looks less severe than GREEN (1 column). In the other phase it is a steady 13-column bar, never blinking. Link down gives '..##..##..##': 1 Hz, not 5 Hz.
proposed_fix: Derive every matrix blink from a multiple of the redraw period. For example, set RED and link-down on the matrix to ((now / kMxPeriodMs) & 1) (2 Hz: on one frame, off the next). Or redraw at a period that divides both half-periods, e.g. kMxPeriodMs = 25. Then correct the comment at lines 1444-1446. Add a harness check that drives matrix_service() at the loop cadence and requires both lit and dark row-7 frames within 2 s.
verifier_evidence: sketch.ino:1452 kMxPeriodMs = 250. matrix_service() (1518-1524) sets last = now and is called only from loop() (1708). g_matrix.draw() is called only there and in matrix_begin(). Row 7 RED uses (now / kAlarmRedHalfMs) & 1 with kAlarmRedHalfMs = 125 (160, 1505). Frames 250 ms apart are 2 half-periods apart, so the parity can never alternate from one frame to the next. Link-down uses kLinkDownHalfMs = 100 (161, 1482): frames advance 2.5 half-periods, giving a 4-frame (1 s) pattern. Reproduced independently with the REAL setup()/loop() on real host time (scratch verify-GS/loop_alias.cpp, sketch compiled with the station harness runtime, 3 runs). RED gave '...####', '...####.......' and '...############': long steady runs, never alternating. Link down gave '..##..##..##..##' (1 Hz, not 5 Hz). This matches the GS 1-ms-step result (0 lit / 80 dark frames in 20 s). Contract section 1 requires 'row 7 alarm level (... RED 13 blinking)'. The comment at 1444-1446 promises 'blinking fast like the ALARM lamp'. The harness check at test_e22.cpp:237 calls matrix_frame() at hand-picked times (mx_time(true,true) = +700 ms, mx_time(false) = +100 ms), never at the redraw cadence, so it cannot see this. The physical ALARM lamp and buzzer (annunciators(), every loop pass, 438/460) blink correctly; only the matrix is wrong. The lamps are owner-wired extras, so the matrix can be the only local indicator. In one phase a RED alarm shows as an EMPTY row 7, which looks milder than GREEN (1 column).
verifier_fix_notes: Minimal: sample the matrix at a period that divides every half-period. gcd(100, 125, 500) = 25, so kMxPeriodMs = 25. Better: compute matrix_frame() every 25 ms but call g_matrix.draw() only when memcmp() shows the frame changed. That keeps exact blink edges at low draw cost. Alternative: derive matrix blinks from a frame counter, e.g. RED = (frame & 1) at 250 ms = 2 Hz, and document the rate. Then fix the comment at 1444-1446 and the '4 Hz redraw' comment. Add a harness check that drives matrix_service() in 1 ms steps for 2 s with RED and with link-down. It must see both lit and dark row-7 frames, and at least 8 transitions per second for link-down.

title: LED-matrix frame-sync row shows LOCK during LOS
description: _matrix_status() sends self.sync.state unconditionally. FrameSynchronizer changes state only when octets arrive (framesync.py _step). After the last CADU of a pass it stays LOCK (or FLYWHEEL) indefinitely; checked: state 'LOCK' after 3 CADUs and still 'LOCK' after a later feed with no data. The M line keeps sending 'L', so row 1 (frame sync LOCK) stays fully lit during LOS. Every other link row is gated on reception within the LOS timeout.
failure_scenario: The pass ends and the LOS timeout expires. Row 0 (AOS) goes dark and rows 3-5 blank, but row 1 stays lit as 'frame sync LOCK' for hours until the next pass. The matrix contradicts itself and reports a lock with no signal.
proposed_fix: In _matrix_status, send sync None or 'SEARCH' when self.rx.los is true (or when no frame arrived within los_timeout_s), e.g. "sync": "PACKET" if packet_mode else (None if rx.los else self.sync.state).
verifier_evidence: gds.py:2268 sends 'sync': self.sync.state with no LOS gating. FrameSynchronizer (framesync.py:81-98) leaves LOCK only through _lose_lock(): a stale partial unit, or more than 3 misses at the expected position. After complete CADUs the buffer is empty, so feed(b'') changes nothing. Noise replies and fault reports are consumed before the state logic (_step 136-139). gds.py never resets self.sync (its only uses are 421, 703-705, 1285, 2268, 2442). Reproduced (verify-GS/los_sync.py, a real GroundStation): after 3 CADUs and about 3000 s of empty feeds, rx.los = True and sync.state = 'LOCK'. _matrix_status gave rssi_recent False and margin None but sync 'LOCK', and matrix_line() produced 'M|L|0|-|?|0|?'. In the sketch, row 1 is lit for kMxLock regardless of g_aos (sketch.ino:1489), so during LOS the matrix shows AOS dark and 'frame sync LOCK' fully lit. The JSON snapshot sync.state (gds.py:2442) has the same stale LOCK.
verifier_fix_notes: In _matrix_status, gate on reception: "sync": "PACKET" if packet_mode else ("SEARCH" if rx.los or not recent else self.sync.state). Sending 'SEARCH' rather than None keeps the field 'known: no lock'. Optionally apply the same gating to the snapshot's sync.state, or call self.sync._lose_lock() on the AOS->LOS transition (that also counts a lock loss, so prefer display gating). Add a test: CADUs, then a time past the LOS timeout, then matrix_line() must not carry 'L'.

title: Radio panels say "[gds] rcu = false" when rcu is true but the RCU path is unavailable
description: _register_check() returns 'not read back: no Radio Control Unit ([gds] rcu = false) ...' whenever radio_mgr or radio_mgr.rcu is None. The same false attribution appears in dashboard.html:1541 ('off ([gds] rcu = false): ...') and 1505 ('needs the Radio Control Unit, [gds] rcu = false') whenever radio.rcu is false. With [gds] rcu = true that also happens when the Router Bridge is unavailable (gds.py:2609-2617, link None, so no _Rcu) or the E22 serial port did not open (radio None, so mgr None, gds.py:2645-2650).
failure_scenario: Checked: cfg['gds']['rcu'] = True, then attach_radio(None, None, 'serial port: ENOENT'). The snapshot gives radio.rcu False and register_check 'not read back: no Radio Control Unit ([gds] rcu = false) ...', while station_io.rcu_configured is True. The operator is sent to station.toml, which is already correct, instead of to the missing bridge package or USB-UART.
proposed_fix: Branch on cfg['gds']['rcu'] when there is no rcu path: rcu = false keeps the current text; rcu = true reports 'configured ([gds] rcu = true) but not available: no Router Bridge / radio serial port not open'. Mirror this in dashboard.html 1505 and 1541 (e.g. from station_io.rcu_configured) and in docs/13:1092-1093.
verifier_evidence: gds.py:2287-2289 returns 'not read back: no Radio Control Unit ([gds] rcu = false) ...' whenever radio_mgr or radio_mgr.rcu is None, without looking at cfg['gds']['rcu']. With rcu = true, Runner (2607-2650) leaves mgr None when the Router Bridge is unavailable (link None, so rcu None, so no RadioManager for an E22, 2645-2650) or when _open_e22() fails (radio None). Reproduced (verify-GS/rcu_word.py): with cfg gds.rcu = True and attach_radio(None, None, 'serial port: ENOENT'), the snapshot gives radio.rcu False, register_check '... ([gds] rcu = false) ...' and station_io.rcu_configured True. dashboard.html:1541 ('off ([gds] rcu = false): ...') and 1505 ('needs the Radio Control Unit, [gds] rcu = false') key only on R.rcu, so they make the same wrong attribution. The wording is new in 3.1; at 13a60c5 the row was a plain 'off'. Mitigation: the same panel shows 'Backend ... UNAVAILABLE' with the error badge, and an ERROR RADIO event is logged, so the real cause is visible nearby. The specific text still sends the operator to station.toml, which is already correct.
verifier_fix_notes: In _register_check, when rm or rm.rcu is None: if not cfg['gds']['rcu'], keep the current text; otherwise return 'not read back: [gds] rcu = true but the Radio Control Unit is not available (' + (self.radio_unavailable or 'no Router Bridge') + ')'. In dashboard.html 1505 and 1541, choose the wording from S.station_io.rcu_configured: 'configured but not available' versus 'off ([gds] rcu = false)'. Update docs/13 to match, and add a test_web case with rcu = true and no backend.

title: D-77 fault_log default never reaches upgraded stations: 3.0 station.toml carries an explicit fault_log = false
description: The 3.0 shipped station.toml contained 'fault_log = false' as a mirrored default (removed in this diff). The App copies station.toml to data/ once, and README 2.6 tells the operator to restore the old data/ folder on update. merge() applies fault_log_default() only when the key is absent, so every station upgraded from 3.0 keeps fault_log false. Selecting model = "E22-400T37S" then leaves the T37S abnormal-status log off (the configuration tool --write and the GDS volatile writes clear REG1 b2), with no hint.
failure_scenario: A 3.0 station is updated to 3.1 by the README procedure and switched to the T37S. regs_from_cfg() writes REG1 b2 = 0, so the module's under-voltage and over-temperature reports never appear, contrary to D-77 ('fault_log defaults to true when model = E22-400T37S').
proposed_fix: Note in the 3.1 upgrade text (README 2.6 / CHANGELOG): delete the old 'fault_log = false' line. Optionally log an INFO at start when model is E22-400T37S and fault_log is explicitly false: 'T37S abnormal-status log off by station.toml'.
verifier_evidence: The 3.0 shipped station.toml (13a60c5) line 62 has 'fault_log = false' as a mirrored default; 98887f5 removes it. merge() applies fault_log_default() only when the key is absent (config.py:143-145). README 2.6 step 3 tells the operator to copy the old data/ (with its station.toml) back, and to compare against the packaged file only 'for new keys', not removed ones. Reproduced (verify-GS/fl.py): the 3.0 file with model switched to E22-400T37S loads under 3.1 with fault_log False and regs_from_cfg REG1 = 0x20 (b2 = 0). The 3.1 file with the same model gives fault_log True and REG1 = 0x24. CHANGELOG has no note. I re-grade to nit: honouring an explicit value in the operator's file is correct config behaviour; the only effect is that the T37S under-voltage and over-temperature reports stay off (diagnostic, no link impact), and one documented line fixes it.
verifier_fix_notes: Add a 3.1 upgrade note (CHANGELOG and README 2.6): 'delete the line fault_log = false from a station.toml copied from 3.0 (it was the old mirrored default; D-77 now derives it from [radio] model)'. Optionally log an INFO at start when model = E22-400T37S and fault_log is explicitly false: 'T37S abnormal-status log off by station.toml'. No code change is required.

title: Station harness checks claim more than they test (4 Hz redraw, millis() wrap)
description: 'loop() redraws the matrix at 4 Hz' requires only >= 2 draws in 600 ms, so it also passes for a redraw on every loop pass or at ~3.4 Hz. 'the RCU age grows across hellos (re-anchored, never wraps with millis())' (line 181) only moves g_rcu_t_ms back by 7 s and 3 s; no millis() wrap is exercised.
failure_scenario: A regression that sets kMxPeriodMs to 0 (redraw every pass) still passes 'at 4 Hz'. A signed or overflowing age computation across the 2^32 ms wrap would not be caught by the 'never wraps' check.
proposed_fix: Count draws over a fixed window and require 2-3 per 600 ms (or check the interval between draws equals kMxPeriodMs). For the wrap, set g_rcu_t_ms = millis() + 0xFFFFF000u - 0xFFFFFFFFu (an anchor just before a wrap) and check that the age stays within the expected small value. Or rename the checks to what they test.
verifier_evidence: Mutation tests on sketch copies under verify-GS/ (the repository was not touched). The 4 Hz part holds: with kMxPeriodMs = 0 (redraw every loop pass), 'loop() redraws the matrix at 4 Hz' still passes, because it only requires draws >= +2 in 600 ms (test_e22.cpp:250-253). The 290 ms variant failed in my run (phase dependent), so the '~3.4 Hz passes' claim is timing dependent, but the lower-bound-only check is real. The millis()-wrap part is largely REFUTED. The harness millis() starts at 0, and an instrumented copy showed millis() = 2561 when 'g_rcu_t_ms -= 7000' runs, so the anchor becomes 4294962857. The uint32 difference (now - g_rcu_t_ms) therefore really crosses the 2^32 boundary, and a wrong difference across that boundary would be caught (incidentally, as long as the check runs within the first 7 s). A mutation that drops the re-anchoring (sketch.ino:346) but keeps the accumulation makes the check FAIL. What is not exercised is an age beyond 49.7 days, which is the property re-anchoring exists for.
verifier_fix_notes: Check the redraw interval exactly. Record the draw times inside run_loop() (or count draws in a 1 s window) and require the gaps to equal kMxPeriodMs within a few ms (e.g. 3-5 draws per 1 s), not just a lower bound. For the RCU age: make the wrap crossing explicit and independent of start-up time. Set g_rcu_t_ms = (uint32_t)millis() - 7000u and comment that it crosses 2^32 when millis() < 7000. Add a long-age case: call rcu_age_s() repeatedly after moving the anchor back 0x7FFF0000 ms twice, and check the age keeps growing past 4294967 s (49.7 days) and saturates at 0x7FFFFFFF. Or rename the check to what it tests.
